draft.title: Physical and economic water scarcity
card: There is not enough water in a place to meet what people need. This can happen where rain is low and rivers or groundwater are small.
There is enough water in or near a place, but people cannot reach it. Dams, pipes, bores or money to build and run them may be missing.
The two kinds can look the same, because people in both go without water. The cause is different: no water, or no way to get it.
The fix depends on the cause. Where water exists, building dams, pipes or bores can help. Where there is not enough water, people must find other supplies or use less.
draft.remember: Physical scarcity is too little water. Economic scarcity is water that people cannot reach.

a.q: A town has a large river nearby, but it has no pumps or pipes to bring the water to homes. What kind of scarcity is this?
opts: Economic scarcity
Physical scarcity
Both kinds at once
Neither kind of scarcity
a.why: The water exists, but people cannot reach it because pipes and pumps are missing. That is economic scarcity. It is not physical scarcity, because the river holds enough water.
a.clue: Does the water exist, and can people get it?

b.q: A remote community in a desert has no rivers, and its only bore has run dry. Which statement best describes its water problem?
opts: Physical scarcity, because there is not enough water
Economic scarcity, because the bore has stopped working
Economic scarcity, because the community is remote
Physical scarcity, because the community has no pipes
b.why: The bore is dry and there are no rivers, so there is not enough water to use. That is physical scarcity. Remoteness and missing pipes are tempting, but they would matter only if water existed and could not be reached.
b.clue: Ask whether more pipes or bores would find any water.

b.best: Physical scarcity, because there is not enough water

problems.detail: The stem says the only bore has run dry but does not say there is no other groundwater. Point 1 teaches that large groundwater stores lie under inland Australia, so a student could argue a deeper or new bore would find water, which would make it economic scarcity. The clue asks whether more bores would find water, but the stem never answers that. Add a line such as 'and there is no groundwater nearby'.

check.summary: The card and question a are accurate and clear. Question b should state that no other groundwater is nearby, because point 1 teaches that inland Australia has large groundwater stores, which makes the 'dry bore = physical scarcity' answer arguable.
